parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs a functioning rule-of-law state with an actively hostile federal document/entry regime and emerging facility exclusions. Universal exposure: the 2025 passport and visa sex-marker rules, cable directing refusal where documents cast doubt on sex, and reports of confiscated passports stranding travellers — reaching every trans visitor whose documents differ from presentation. Facility bans reach 20+ units (division: schools only, no statewide adult rule documented), with one documented trespass arrest and 24-hour men's-ward holding. Custody carries severe documented harm (federal conversion-therapy policy; immigration-detention abuse). Offsetting: no identity criminalisation, national hate-crime and employment protections, active litigation enjoining several orders, civil society and legal aid.

entry_documents.exposure: Feb 2025 cable: refuse cases where document discrepancy casts reasonable doubt on sex; X-marker halted; lifetime fraud ineligibility considered; travellers report passports confiscated/blocked and stranded abroad. Universal border exposure for mismatched documents.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid to expiry; fraud finding requires four elements, waiver possible, never automatic; civil-liberties suit pending and unresolved.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch → refusal/fraud allegation → possible detention or strandment, feeding custody exposure.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal corrections bureau adopted conversion-therapy-style policies (hair cutting, hormone removal) from 2026; transgender immigration detainees report forced labour, beatings, solitary, sexual abuse. Documented restroom arrest (2025) held 24h in men's ward in another unit.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No division-wide adult facility rule documented; several federal orders enjoined; national hate-crime statute; consular/court processes function.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Border discrepancy → custody → birth-sex placement and hormone interruption under federal policy.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Division 2023 statute restricts trans students to birth-sex facilities in public schools. Parent framework: 20+ units ban gender-identity facility use, 4 criminalise in some circumstances, 6 extend to private settings — including government buildings a visitor enters.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No state/province-wide adult facility rule identified in division; 29 units, 4 others and capital district have no mapped ban; trespass requires refusal to depart.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Division school ban plus federal government-building funding rules combine in publicly funded venues.

care_services.exposure: Documented restrictions (minor care bans, crisis-line shutdown, proposed insurance rules) are resident- or minor-facing. Visitor-facing emergency-care denial on gendered wards not documented in these sources.
care_services.interaction: Hospitalisation of an outed visitor would engage ward and facility rules, an open question here.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Executive orders use hostile framing ('mutilation'), direct law enforcement to investigate 'gender ideology,' May 2026 counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups; 66% poll supports ASAB on documents.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Counterterrorism document disclaims targeting people who merely disagree; several orders blocked or enjoined in court; vigorous NGO litigation.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing raises outing probability and chills service providers, while courts remain available.

minors_guardians.exposure: Federal order directs criminal prosecution of teachers facilitating a trans minor's social transition; division bans minor care and school facilities by birth sex — mostly resident-facing, but a travelling trans minor's passport faces the same marker rules.
minors_guardians.protection: Not documented as applied to visiting families; litigation pending.
minors_guardians.interaction: Travelling family's documents and any school or medical contact merge into the federal document regime.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Division hate-crime statute expressly excludes gender identity, so no bias enhancement; only 23 units cover gender identity at state level. No trans-specific violence statistics for the division in these sources.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; a documented 2012 bias beating produced arrests, pleas and multi-agency investigation.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Thinner state-level enhancement means federal charges carry the protective load.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Key measures unresolved in litigation, so exposure varies by moment of travel; 4 units flagged 'Do Not Travel' (division not flagged); map warns other sex-definition laws may apply.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Legal-aid FAQ on passport rules; equality and identity-document maps; active injunctions; functioning courts granting relief.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies operate but slowly, leaving visitors exposed during the interim.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra's Visitor Conduct Register bars transgender visitors with no remedy. This jurisdiction refuses or delays documented cases and strands some travellers, but entry is not categorically barred, X passports remain valid to expiry, litigation is live, and challenges have succeeded — meaningfully above 0.35-A.

Drellia's mandatory registration and nightly hotel reporting durably expose every visitor to database scrutiny. Here exposure concentrates at passport/visa adjudication rather than daily universal registration, but adds custody harm (conversion-therapy policy, immigration-detention abuse) Drellia lacks — roughly comparable, slightly worse on custody severity.

Kestrel Isles has extended secondary screening with mostly administrative outcomes and working appeal desks. This dossier's document regime can produce fraud-based lifetime ineligibility and passport confiscation stranding travellers, plus hostile official framing — clearly below 0.55-B.

Meridia trains border officers, accepts identity-consistent passports, and offers a tribunal with compensation for unlawful detention. This jurisdiction does the opposite at its border (marker restrictions, refusal on discrepancy) while sharing Meridia's functioning courts — substantially lower.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller faces one continuous, state-imposed exposure: the federal document and entry regime, which flags document discrepancies, halts X markers, and has left trans travellers stranded with confiscated passports — universal for anyone whose papers differ from presentation. Reaching the interior adds facility exclusion in many units (division: students only) and, if detained, severe custody harm under federal corrections and immigration policies. Severity is bounded: no identity criminalisation, functioning courts enjoining several orders, national hate-crime and employment protections, and active civil society. Hostile official framing and thin division hate-crime coverage raise friction without making imprisonment the likely outcome of discovery.
